subject: PayGrid model-fit eval — parity thresholds & next steps
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sara.lim@paygrid.com, tom.nguyen@paygrid.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary: You showed the invoice parsing and QA flows — the two priority evaluation paths are (1) line-item extraction for invoice ingestion and (2) answer-generation for invoice dispute triage.
- Recommended initial models to evaluate: Redwood-open-1.3 (quantized) and Redwood-prop-1.0 (baseline) for parity checks.
- Metric priorities: exact-match for line items (primary), F1 for entity spans (secondary), and human-review regression rate for end-to-end dispute triage.

Action items we covered: 
1) PayGrid to share a small-sample benchmark (50 invoices) and redaction rules by EOD Friday (you).
2) Redwood to share a prompt set + recommended evaluation harness and an initial parity benchmark (us).
3) Schedule a 60-min follow-up for demoing model outputs and reviewing thresholds next week.

I attached an initial parity benchmark CSV and a draft prompt set to get you started. Also linking our parity benchmark doc and the HubSpot deal below.

Attachments: paygrid_parity_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v2.txt
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks, https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4821

Proposed follow-up times: Tue 6/1 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 6/2 13:00-14:00 PT — what works for you?

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@paygrid.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.nguyen@paygrid.com
Date: 2027-05-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — recap & next steps

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap. We'll get the 50-invoice sample over by Friday and include the redaction rules (PII, account numbers). A couple quick clarifications: 

- For the "Redwood-prop-1.0" baseline, are you referring to the proprietary model we saw in the hosted demo last quarter? We want to understand if parity tests compare open models against that hosted baseline or against our current in-house rule-based extractor.
- For the parity CSV you attached, can you include a column for business-impact severity (low/med/high) so stakeholders can prioritize failures?

Tue 6/1 10:00 PT works for us for the follow-up. Looking forward to the prompt set.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Data & ML, PayGrid

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sara.lim@paygrid.com, tom.nguyen@paygrid.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-31T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — recap & next steps

Sara —

Thanks — quick answers inline and attached updated artifacts.

- "Redwood-prop-1.0": yes, this is the hosted proprietary baseline we showed in the demo (server-side model with our tuned safety and post-processing). We'll compare both: (A) your current rule-based extractor (to show lift from rules) and (B) prop-1.0 (to evaluate open vs proprietary parity). We'll label columns accordingly in the CSV.
- Added a "business_impact" column to the CSV (see paygrid_parity_benchmarks.csv).

Attached: paygrid_parity_benchmarks.csv (updated), prompt_set_v2.txt (example prompts + expected JSON schema), short README for the harness. Also included a link to our public parity benchmark write-up.

Recommended evaluation plan (short):
1) Run Redwood-open-1.3 (q4) and Redwood-prop-1.0 against the 50-invoice sample.
2) Collect exact-match / F1 / human-review regression rate.
3) Apply a parity threshold: for line-item extraction, we recommend open-model must be within 3 percentage points exact-match of prop-1.0 to pass parity for a pilot; for end-to-end triage we recommend a <5% human-review regression increase. These are suggestions we can adapt with your stakeholders.

Link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/open-vs-prop-2027

Proposed meeting: Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 PT — I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Lauren

Attachments: paygrid_parity_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v2.txt

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: parity thresholds + quality-regression note

Lauren —

Thanks for leading this. A couple internal flags before the call: 

- The 3-point exact-match threshold is aggressive on noisy OCR inputs; recommend we run an OCR-normalization pass and include a fallback post-processing rule for numeric canonicalization so prop advantage isn't purely due to normalization. Note this is an implementation-level mitigation, not a change to parity definition.
- For triage/regression, if PayGrid is particularly sensitive to false positives (high business impact), we should propose an A/B gating strategy where we route a percentage of traffic to open model with automatic rollback on 7-day regression > 4%.
- Please be ready to discuss compute/latency tradeoffs — quantized open models may need different batching to meet PayGrid SLOs.

I'll join the call and take notes on acceptance criteria.

-Marissa
Principal Applied ML, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sara.lim@paygrid.com, tom.nguyen@paygrid.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-02T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — recap & next steps

Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the sample and for confirming the 6/1 meeting — calendar invite sent. Finalizing the mutual action plan attached (mutual_action_plan.docx) — high-level next steps below and acceptance thresholds we proposed: 

Mutual action plan (high level):
- 6/2: Run initial parity eval on 50 invoices (Redwood runs; PayGrid to validate PII redactions).
- 6/7: Review results and agree on pilot acceptance thresholds.
- 6/14: Start 2-week pilot with 10% traffic to open model, monitoring human-review regression and latency.

Proposed acceptance thresholds (suggested):
- Line-item exact-match: open within 3 percentage points of prop-1.0 (primary).
- Entity F1: within 4 percentage points.
- Human-review regression (end-to-end triage): <5% increase vs baseline.
- Latency: P95 inference latency must be <= 350ms with our recommended batching profile.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx
Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4821

If these look reasonable we'll finalize and surface to your procurement contact for next steps on pilot pricing.

Thanks — see you on the call,

Lauren
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
